method: every counted row is a CONSERVATIVE PATH UPPER BOUND on executed instructions per call; every instruction in the span counts, INCLUDING operand-free instructions (ret, and the stp frame); branch targets matched for Darwin LBB and ELF .L; loop-bearing symbols body x trip + remainder
counting_convention: an instruction is any line whose first token is an opcode with or without operands; `.` directives excluded; the rule is applied identically to every span, so _v15r_reset_hist is 16 (15 + ret)

escape.measured_fire_rate_source: evidence/census-v15t.json:detector_fires/steps_executed (executed-step denominator; the budgeted-step rate in the same file is strictly smaller, so this is conservative)

inversions.policy: NO batching is claimed.  Every affine addition on the shipped path calls v15q_add, which performs one Fermat inversion; successive walk steps, the SMALL[v] = SMALL[v-1] + Q recurrence and the escape double-and-add ladders all consume earlier affine results, so no dependency-respecting batch exists.  Each add is charged its flat add price AND one full inversion, with no scheduling premise.
inversions.withdrawn_premise: v15r's 67-step refill, 2048-add init batch and 66-add escape batch are withdrawn; the conservative single-inversion price replaces them

recovery_bound.stopping_cap: each worker halts at the FIRST collision it reports (v15o_report returns the resident label at the matching write) and makes exactly ONE solve attempt; a failed solve is the deterministic failure branch, never a retry
recovery_bound.candidate_pair_law: candidate pairs = sum over reports of P(match) x pool occupancy; every delivered pair belongs to exactly one worker, and a worker stops at its first delivered pair, so the sum is bounded by the worker count 2^20

pool_addressing.slot_rule: slot = hash(x) mod n_slots, n_slots = 2^34 per shard (fixed cap)

capacity_model.law: the pool holds EVERY reported record at the measured load factor, so the retained-match count H x M / N6 with M = slots x fill is the all-history birthday term, not a thin subsample of it
capacity_model.arithmetic: slots_total = reports / 0.5 = 2^127.508; shards = ceil(slots_total / 2^34) = 2^93.508; per-shard load = reports / (shards x 2^34) = 2^-1.000
capacity_model.retention_charged_into_work: a retained fraction r multiplies BOTH H and M, so the expected match count scales by r^2; the arrival budget is therefore divided by r (one full power of conservatism), giving S_charged = ceil(S / r) = 241941295532617856272805037518322888088 arrivals and a walk term 0.957143 bits above the un-retained S
capacity_model.allocation_model: demand-based: a shard is materialised only when a record maps into it, so allocated <= slots_total x 96 B; the pool is charged at its declared capacity
capacity_model.note: this is the honest answer to the reviewer's H x M / N6 objection: v15r's 2^62-slot pool against 2^126.45 reports made M/H = 2^-64.45, so no all-history birthday term existed; v15t makes M >= H at load 0.5 and pays the retention factor in work

storage_model.worker_state_provenance: scripts/rec_layout.h:worker_t, sizeof machine-derived by scripts/layout_assert.c with _Static_assert on every offset (264 = rec_t 88 + a,c 64 + prev0,prev1 64 + minx 32 + rep,win 16)
storage_model.batch_prefix_provenance: Montgomery prefix array, WORKER_BATCH=67 x 64 B per worker (two 32-byte field-element arrays)
storage_model.peak_row: sum(workers x worker_state + prefix scratch + record_pool + shard_metadata + jump_table + code + advice)

mu_note: priced at 2.842 (measured on the long-trail v15q census; this round's normalized-budget census re-measures 1.020, so the price is conservative)
